setup.title: Let’s get your computer ready
setup.subtitle: Studio needs a few free tools. We check each one and show you what to do if something is missing.
setup.skipHint: You can finish setup later from Settings, but you can’t build until everything is ready.

confirmInstall.title: Install {{tool}}?
confirmInstall.body: Studio will run exactly this command and show you the progress. By choosing “Run command” you also accept the terms of the package and its source:
confirmInstall.note: Windows may ask for permission. Studio never installs anything without asking first.

login.hint: A browser window opens so you can sign in to Claude yourself. If it asks for a code, paste it in the terminal below. Studio never sees your password or token.
login.needsClaude: Install Claude Code first, then you can sign in.
login.waiting: Waiting for you to sign in…

git.name: Git
git.why: Keeps a history of every change so you can always go back.

windows: Choose “Install for me”, or download Git for Windows from the page we open.
Run the installer and keep the suggested options.
Come back here and choose “Check again”.
macos: Follow the pop-up to install the developer tools.
Come back here and choose “Check again”.
linux: Install Git with your package manager, for example: sudo apt install git
Come back here and choose “Check again”.

flutter.name: Flutter SDK
flutter.why: The toolkit that turns your app into real iOS and Android apps.

windows: Open the install guide and pick Windows, then Android.
Download the Flutter SDK zip and unzip it somewhere simple, like C:\src\flutter (no spaces).
Add the folder flutter\bin to your PATH (the guide shows how).
macos: Open the install guide and pick macOS.
Download the Flutter SDK and unzip it in your home folder.
Add flutter/bin to your PATH (the guide shows how).
linux: Open the install guide and pick Linux.
Download the Flutter SDK and extract it in your home folder.
Add flutter/bin to your PATH (the guide shows how).

issues.dart_old: Your Flutter includes Dart {{dart}}. Studio needs Dart 3.9 or newer (Flutter 3.35 or newer).

updateSteps: Open a terminal and run: flutter upgrade

android.name: Android toolchain
android.why: Lets Studio build and test Android apps. Needed before you can publish to Google Play.

issues.no_sdk: Android Studio (which includes the Android SDK) isn’t installed yet.
issues.licenses: The Android licenses still need to be accepted. This is a one-time step.
issues.cmdline_tools: One Android component (command-line tools) is missing.
issues.needs_flutter: Install the Flutter SDK first. Then we can check Android.
issues.other: Flutter found a problem with the Android setup. Open the details to see what.

no_sdk: Download Android Studio from the page we open and install it with the default options.
Start Android Studio once and let it finish downloading the Android SDK.
Come back here and choose “Check again”.
licenses: Choose “Accept licenses” (after ticking the box). Studio does the rest and checks it for you.
cmdline_tools: Open Android Studio, then Settings, then Android SDK, then the SDK Tools tab.
Tick “Android SDK Command-line Tools”, press Apply and wait for it to finish.
Come back here and choose “Check again”.
other: Open the technical details below and look at the lines marked with ✗ or !.
Fix them (Android Studio’s SDK Manager fixes most), then choose “Check again”.
needs_flutter: Finish the Flutter SDK step above first.

license.agree: I agree to the Android SDK terms.
license.agreedBefore: You agreed to the Android SDK terms earlier. Studio accepts the licenses for you.
license.checking: All licenses accepted. Checking that everything works…
license.stalled: This is taking longer than usual…
license.stalledHelp: Nothing has happened for a while. Studio is looking for the cause.
license.allDone_one: Done: {{count}} license accepted and checked, in {{seconds}} seconds.
license.allDone_other: Done: {{count}} licenses accepted and checked, in {{seconds}} seconds.
license.alreadyDone: The licenses were already accepted. Everything checks out.
license.acceptedButDoctor: The licenses are accepted, but Flutter still reports a problem with the Android setup. Open the technical details.
license.failed: The licenses couldn’t be accepted yet.

problems.java_missing: Java wasn’t found. It comes with Android Studio; install Android Studio first.
problems.java_broken: Java was found but doesn’t start. Reinstalling Android Studio fixes this.
problems.sdk_missing: The Android SDK wasn’t found. Install Android Studio and open it once.
problems.cmdline_tools_missing: The Android command-line tools are missing. In Android Studio: Settings, Android SDK, SDK Tools, tick “Android SDK Command-line Tools”.
problems.no_network: Google’s download server can’t be reached. Check your internet connection or VPN.

claude.name: Claude Code
claude.why: The AI that writes your app. It runs on your own Claude account.

windows: Choose “Install for me”, or follow the install guide on the page we open.
Restart Studio so it can find Claude.
macos: Open the install guide and follow the macOS steps.
Restart Studio so it can find Claude.
linux: Open the install guide and follow the Linux steps.
Restart Studio so it can find Claude.

claudeLogin.name: Claude account
claudeLogin.why: You sign in yourself through the official Claude Code. Studio only checks whether you are signed in.

unknown.title: Something unexpected happened
unknown.fix: Try again. If it keeps happening, restart Studio and check the log file in Settings.

db.title: Studio couldn’t read its own data
db.fix: Restart Studio. If this keeps happening, your projects are still safe in their folders; check the log file in Settings.

io.title: Studio couldn’t access a file or folder
io.fix: Check that the folder exists and isn’t read-only or open in another program, then try again.

not_found.title: We couldn’t find that
not_found.fix: It may have been removed. Go back to your projects and try again.

invalid.title: That doesn’t look right
invalid.fix: Check what you entered and try again.

tool_missing.title: {{tool}} isn’t available yet
tool_missing.fix: Open setup to install it. Studio walks you through it.

command_failed.title: A tool reported a problem
command_failed.fix: Open setup to check your tools, then try again. The technical details are in the log file (Settings).

timeout.title: This is taking too long
timeout.fix: Check your internet connection and try again.

path_exists.title: That folder already exists
path_exists.fix: Pick another name or another projects folder in Settings.

unsafe.title: Studio stopped to protect your files
unsafe.fix: That folder isn’t a Studio project inside your projects folder. Nothing was deleted.

pty.title: The terminal couldn’t start
pty.fix: Close the terminal and try again. If it still fails, restart Studio.

keychain.title: Studio couldn’t reach your computer’s keychain
keychain.fix: Unlock your keychain or password manager and try again. Studio only stores secrets there, never in your project.

unsupported.title: Not available yet
unsupported.fix: This part is planned for a later version of Studio. Everything else keeps working.

rejected.title: That value was not accepted
rejected.fix: This value was not accepted. Check it and try again.

device.title: Run on your own phone
device.intro: See your app on a real phone while you build. Pick your phone below, or follow the steps if it doesn’t show up.
device.noneBody: Connect your phone and follow the steps below, then choose “Look again”.
device.stepsTitle: How to connect an Android phone
usb: On your phone open Settings, then About phone, and tap “Build number” seven times to turn on Developer options.
Open Settings, then Developer options, and turn on “USB debugging”.
Connect the phone to this computer with a USB cable.
On the phone, tap “Allow” when it asks to trust this computer.
Come back here and choose “Look again”.
wireless_steps: Put the phone on the same Wi-Fi network as this computer.
In Developer options turn on “Wireless debugging” and open it.
Tap “Pair device with pairing code”. In a terminal run: adb pair <address:port from the phone>, then type the code.
Then run: adb connect <address:port shown on the Wireless debugging screen>.
device.ios: iPhones can only be used from a Mac with Xcode. Studio will support this together with iOS publishing.

pick.layer: Drag to draw a box around what you want to change. The app itself does not react here.
pick.pageBody: Everything you ask applies to this whole page. Drag a box in the app to change only what is inside it. Trying out the app is what “Test run” is for.
pick.elementBody: Claude only changes what is inside the marked box and leaves the rest of the page alone.
pick.tooSmallBody: Hold the mouse button down and pull to cover what you want to change.
pick.looking: Looking at what is in the box…
pick.exceeded: Claude also changed something outside the marked box.

preview.loadingBody: Your app is being prepared. The first time can take a minute or two.

notLinked.title: This page isn’t connected to the app yet
notLinked.body: Nobody can reach “{{screen}}” from the app yet, so there is nothing to show here.
notLinked.prompt: Connect the screen {{screen}} to the app: add a route for it in the router and a sensible link or button to it from another screen. Only this screen. Keep STUDIO.md up to date.

failure.flutterMissingBody: The preview needs Flutter on this computer.
failure.startFailedBody: Something in the app stops it from building.
failure.crashedBody: It stopped several times in a row.

screens.noneHint: Ask Claude to add one. Screens are widgets whose name ends in Screen or Page.
screens.hint: Click a screen to talk about it in the chat.
screens.addPrompt: Add a new screen to the app. Ask me what it should show if that isn’t clear, add it to the navigation, and update STUDIO.md.
screens.linkPrompt: Look at the screens and how they connect. Suggest and then add sensible navigation between screens that are not reachable yet, and update STUDIO.md.

tree.hint: Click a page to see it in the preview and talk about it in the chat. Drag pages onto folders to sort them.
tree.deleteBody: The pages inside stay in your app and move up one level. Only the folder in this list goes away.

theme.title: Colors
theme.applied: Color updated. The preview refreshes by itself.
theme.notWired: This app has its own theme code, so Studio’s theme isn’t connected. Ask Claude to connect it.
theme.wirePrompt: Make MaterialApp use AppTheme.light and AppTheme.dark from lib/app_theme.dart, and remove any colors that are set by hand elsewhere.
theme.fontHelp: Studio adds the font and uses it everywhere. The preview updates by itself.
theme.kitHelp: Studio applies this style to buttons, cards and the app bar across all screens.
theme.fontPrompt: Use the font “{{font}}” for the whole app (add it with the google_fonts package or bundle it as an asset) and make sure the theme file uses it.
theme.kitPrompt: Give the whole app a “{{kit}}” look and feel. Pick a suitable Flutter package or theme settings, apply it consistently on every screen, and keep using AppTheme for colors.
theme.deviation: The theme was changed by hand. Choose a color to put Studio’s theme back.
theme.pubGetFailed: The font needs a download that didn’t work. Check your internet connection and choose the font again.

data.title: Data and login
data.intro: Choose where your app keeps its data and how people sign in. You use your own account; Studio never holds your keys.

local.name: On the phone
local.desc: A local database. No account, no server.

data.authHelp: Only relevant if people have accounts.
data.supabaseRefHelp: The part before .supabase.co in your project URL.
data.tokenHelp: Lets Claude set up tables and rules in your project. Studio keeps it in your computer’s keychain, never in your project.
data.firebaseNote: Claude uses your own Firebase login (firebase-tools). If you aren’t signed in yet, ask Claude and it tells you the command.
data.accountDeletion: The app lets people delete their account
data.accountDeletionHelp: Google Play and the App Store both require this when an app has accounts.
data.setupHint: Studio adds the packages, start code and sign-in screen itself. No chat needed.
data.applied: Data and login are set up.
data.appliedBody_one: Studio set this up itself ({{count}} file). No chat needed.
data.appliedBody_other: Studio set this up itself ({{count}} files). No chat needed.
data.pubAddFailed: The packages could not be downloaded. Check your internet connection and choose “Set up” again.
data.accountDeletionAuto: “Delete my account” is built in, so that store question is already answered.
data.customTables: Design my own tables with Claude
data.customTablesHint: Optional. Only needed if your app stores its own kind of data.

notes.auth_social_manual: Sign in with Google or Apple needs settings from Google or Apple. Studio sets up email and anonymous sign-in; ask Claude for the rest if you need it.
notes.firebase_options: Firebase: sign in once on your computer (run “flutterfire configure”) so the platform settings exist.
notes.supabase_delete_sql: Supabase: run studio/data/supabase_delete_user.sql once in your project (SQL editor) so “delete my account” works.
notes.local_no_accounts: A local database has no accounts, so the login methods you ticked are ignored.
notes.data_main_not_wired: Your main.dart has its own form, so Studio didn’t change it. Call initStudioData() before runApp.
notes.data_router_not_wired: Your router has its own form, so the /login page isn’t connected yet.

warnings.not_square: The image isn’t square. Studio used the middle part.
warnings.no_platforms: No Android, iOS or web folders were found.

assets.splashLogo: Show my app icon in the middle
assets.splashNoIcon: Choose an app icon above first.

versions.title: Versions
versions.intro: Every change by Claude is saved as a snapshot, so you can always go back.
versions.nothing: Nothing changed since the last snapshot.
versions.restoreBody: The app returns to how it was then. Nothing is lost: your current state is saved first and the old version becomes a new snapshot you can undo again.
versions.changelogHelp: Changes since the last release, from your snapshots.
versions.changelogPrompt:
Write or update CHANGELOG.md for version {{version}} in plain language for app users (short bullet points, newest first). Base it on these changes:
{{changes}}

version.title: App version
version.nextChanges: The next upload automatically gets version {{version}}, build {{build}}.
version.nextSame: The next upload uses these numbers.
version.auto: Studio keeps this in line with your app and raises the version and build number by itself before each upload, because the stores only accept higher numbers.
version.dialogBody: Only do this if you need a specific number. The build number must be higher than the one you last uploaded.
version.versionInvalid: Use three numbers with dots, like 1.2.0
version.buildInvalid: Use a whole number of {{min}} or higher

listing.title: Store page
listing.intro: What people see in Google Play.
listing.name: App title
listing.writePrompt: Write the store page texts for this app in the app’s own language: a title of at most 30 characters, a short description of at most 80 characters and a full description of at most 4000 characters, plus a fitting category (one of: tools, productivity, lifestyle, health, education, entertainment, games, finance, social, business). Base it on STUDIO.md and the screens, then save it with the Studio tool set_store_listing.

listing.questionsHelp: Google Play asks these in its privacy and rating forms. Answer them here, then fill the same answers in on the Play Console.

summary.location: Declare location use in Data safety and explain it to users.

summary.none: No special declarations needed beyond the basics.

listing.consoleDone: I filled these in in Google Play Console

legal.title: Legal
legal.intro: A privacy policy and terms are required in the store. Claude writes them from what your app does; you put them online and add the links.
legal.generatePrompt: Write a privacy policy and terms of use for this app in plain language, in the app’s own language, based on STUDIO.md, the data choices (.studio/publish.json) and the permissions. Save them as legal/privacy-policy.md and legal/terms.md and also as simple standalone HTML pages legal/privacy-policy.html and legal/terms.html. Use the contact email from the store page. Don’t invent facts about the app: ask me if something is unclear. Remind me this is not legal advice.
legal.docsReady: Both documents exist in the legal folder
hostSteps: Create a free GitHub account (or use any website you control).
Make a new public repository and upload the two .html files from the legal folder.
In the repository settings turn on GitHub Pages. After a minute your pages are online.
Copy the two web addresses and paste them below.
legal.hostedChecked: I opened both links and the pages are online
legal.disclaimer: These texts are a starting point and not legal advice. Have them checked if your app handles sensitive data.
legal.accountDeletion: The app lets people delete their account
legal.accountDeletionHelp: Needed when people can sign in.

signing.title: Accounts and signing
signing.intro: Android apps must be signed with a key that only you have. Studio creates it and keeps its password in your keychain.
signing.backup: Back this file up somewhere safe. If you lose it you can’t update your app anymore.
signing.noKeytool: Java’s keytool wasn’t found. It comes with Android Studio; install it in setup first.
signing.playHelp: You need a Google Play developer account (one-time fee) and a service account key so Studio can upload for you.
playSteps: Create your developer account at play.google.com/console.
In Play Console open Setup, then API access, and create a service account.
Give it permission to release apps, then create a JSON key and download it.
Paste the contents of that JSON file below. Studio keeps it in your keychain.
signing.accountReady: My Google Play developer account is ready
signing.fastlaneMissing: Not installed. Install it from docs.fastlane.tools, then check again.
signing.closedBody: Google currently requires new personal developer accounts to run a closed test with enough testers for a number of days before an app can go to production (at the time of writing 12 testers for 14 days; check the Play Console for the current rule). Upload to the internal or closed track first.
signing.iosBody: Publishing for iOS needs a Mac or a cloud build service and an Apple Developer account. Studio will support it later. The checklist already covers everything except this last step.

release.title: Release
release.intro: Studio builds your app bundle and uploads it to Google Play as a draft on a test track. You finish the release in Play Console.
release.confirmBox: I checked everything and want to release this version
release.confirmBody: Studio builds the release bundle and uploads it as a draft to the {{track}} track. Nothing goes live to the public: you finish the release in Play Console.
release.done: Uploaded! Open Play Console to finish and roll out the release.
release.failed: This step failed. The log below shows why.
release.needKey: Add your Google Play key first (see Accounts).

publish.fixAllHelp_other: Studio can fill in {{count}} things for you right now.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.intro: Switch on what your app needs. Studio then asks for the keys it needs, and keeps them safe.

off.title: Switch off {{name}}?
off.body: You can keep the saved secrets in case you switch it on again, or delete them from this computer.
off.globalNote: Secrets that belong to your account (not just this app) stay in place either way, because other apps may use them.
off.keep: Switch off and keep the secrets
off.delete: Switch off and delete this app's secrets

needs.title: {{name}} needs more
needs.body: {{name}} works together with: {{deps}}. Switch that on as well?

secrets.title: Secrets
secrets.intro: Everything here stays on this computer, in a safe place. Claude and the chat never see the values.
secrets.publicVsSecret: Some values are public and some are secret. Public values (like a web address) may be in your app. Secret values (like a password or key file) must never be: anyone could use them. Studio keeps both in its own safe, and checks your files so secrets never end up in your app or online.
secrets.copied: Copied. Paste it where you need it.
secrets.dropHere: Drop the file here ({{types}}) or browse for it.

generate.intro: Studio creates a signing key and fills in the passwords for you. You only need a name.

confirm.showBody: Make sure nobody is looking at your screen. {{name}} is hidden again after {{s}} seconds.
confirm.copyBody: {{name}} will be placed on your clipboard. Paste it only where it belongs.
confirm.replaceBody: The old value is removed and cannot be brought back.
confirm.replaceKeystore: The old signing key is removed and cannot be brought back. Without it you can no longer update your published app. Only continue if you have a backup.
confirm.deleteBody: The value is removed from this computer and cannot be brought back.
confirm.deleteKeystore: Without this signing key you can no longer update your published app. Only delete it if you have a backup.

errors.empty: This field is empty. Type or paste the value, then press Save.
errors.multiline: This must be a single line. Check that you copied only the value.
errors.too_short: That looks too short (at least {{detail}} characters). Copy the whole value again.
errors.not_an_option: Pick one of the options in the list.
errors.pattern: That does not look right. Copy the value again from the website, without extra spaces, and try once more.
errors.secret_in_public_field: This is the SECRET key, which must never be inside an app. Put it in the "Secret key" field, and use the publishable key here.
errors.file_type: This is not the right type of file. Choose a file of type {{detail}}.
errors.content: This file does not contain what we expect. Download it again from the service and choose that file.
errors.json_invalid: This file cannot be read as a key file. Download it again, and do not open or edit it first.
errors.json_missing: This key file is missing a part ({{detail}}). Create a new key and download it again.
errors.json_wrong: This is not the right kind of key file ({{detail}}). Check that you downloaded a service account key.
errors.too_large: This file is too large to be a key file (at most 512 KB). Choose the original file you downloaded.
errors.not_text: This file cannot be read here. Choose the original file you downloaded.
errors.passphrase_short: Use a passphrase of at least {{detail}} characters.
errors.backup_unreadable: The backup could not be opened. Check the passphrase and that this is the right file.
errors.vault_has_value: Studio already has a value for this ({{detail}}). Delete that one first if you want to replace it.
errors.generic: This value was not accepted. Check it and try again.

testResult.checked_locally: The details look right. (A live check with the service follows in a later version.)
testResult.invalid_credentials: The service says these details are not valid. Check the key and replace it.
testResult.forbidden: The service refuses this key. Check its permissions and try again.
testResult.unreachable: Could not reach the service. Check your internet connection and the web address.
testResult.incomplete: Fill in all required fields first.
testResult.file_invalid: A saved file is no longer valid. Replace it.
testResult.not_found: The service did not find this. Check the web address or ID.
testResult.rate_limited: The service asks you to wait. Try again in a minute.
testResult.unexpected: The service gave an unexpected answer. Try again later.

secrets.expired: This key has expired. Create a new one and replace it here.
secrets.expiresIn: This key expires in {{count}} day(s). Create a new one before then.

empty.title: No secrets needed yet
empty.body: Secrets appear here for each integration you switch on. Switch on what your app needs first.

backup.title: Back-up
backup.why: Make an encrypted back-up, especially of your Android signing key. If that key is lost, nobody can recover it and you can never update your published app again. Keep the file and the passphrase in two different safe places.
backup.exportHelp: Choose a passphrase you can remember. Without it the back-up cannot be opened, and we cannot recover it for you.
backup.importHelp: Choose the back-up file and enter its passphrase.
backup.mismatch: The two passphrases are not the same.

leaks.title: A secret was found in your files
leaks.body: Studio paused saving versions and publishing, because a secret in your files could end up online or inside your app. Fix it below, then replace the key with a new one if it was already saved before.
leaks.tracked: This was already saved in your history. Create a new key and replace it.
leaks.moved: Moved to the safe and removed from your files.
leaks.confirmTitle: Move this file to the safe?
leaks.confirmBody: {{file}} will be stored safely in Studio and removed from your project folder.

kind.known_secret: One of your saved secrets is written in this file.
kind.private_key: A private key is written in this file.
kind.token: A secret key or token is written in this file.
kind.service_role_key: A Supabase secret (service_role) key is written here. It must never be inside an app.
kind.secret_file: A key file is stored in the project folder.
kind.service_account_file: A service account key file is stored in the project folder.
kind.env_file: An .env file with secrets is in the project folder.
kind.secret_in_app_assets: A secret file is listed as part of the app, so it would ship inside the app.

purchases.title: Purchases
purchases.intro: Define what people can buy, what it unlocks and how the paywall looks. Studio sets up the code and guides you through the stores. Prices in your app always come from the store.

kindHelp.subscription: Renews every week, month or year.
kindHelp.consumable: Can be bought again and again, like coins.

stores.title: Set up in the stores
stores.intro: Studio can’t create products in the stores for you yet, so you do that part yourself. Use exactly the IDs below: they can never be changed afterwards. Then tell Studio when it’s done.
stores.allCreated: All products are created in the stores.

products.title: Products
products.help: The price you enter is only the base price used to create the product in the stores. In your app, people always see the real price from the store.
products.noneHint: Add a one-time purchase or a subscription to get started.

product.intro: Pick the type, give it a name and a base price. Studio suggests the rest.
product.name: Name
product.unlockHelp: A short word for the access it gives, like pro.
product.priceHelp: Only used to create it in the stores.
product.idWarning: Product IDs are permanent in the stores. After you add this product to the app you can no longer change the ID.
product.idLocked: This product is already in the app or a store, so its ID and type can’t change anymore.

problems.id_invalid: Use lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.
problems.id_duplicate: Another product already uses this ID.

provider.label: How purchases are handled in the app
provider.revenueCatWhy: RevenueCat takes care of renewals, restoring purchases and who has access. It needs a free RevenueCat account and its public key in the secrets.
provider.iapWhy: The official package is enough for simple one-time purchases and needs no extra account.

gating.title: What is behind the paywall
gating.describeHelp: Describe it in your own words, for example: unlimited saved games and exporting.
gating.adjustHint: Remove anything that shouldn’t be locked, then approve.

paywall.title: Paywall

placements.lockedFeature: When someone taps a locked feature

paywall.headline: Headline
paywall.bodyExample: Unlock all features and support the app.
paywall.styleHelp: The paywall uses your app’s colours, fonts and components.
paywall.noProducts: Add a product to see it here.
paywall.realPriceNote: This is a preview. In the app the real price and currency come from the store, never from a fixed number.
paywall.tweakHelp: Claude changes the paywall settings, for example: calmer, bigger button.

options.title: The options as the app shows them
options.note: The real price shown in the app comes from the store.

risks.price_increase: Raising the price of “{{product}}” affects people who already subscribe.
risks.remove_with_buyers: “{{product}}” already has buyers. Removing it from the app doesn’t remove it from the stores, and buyers keep what they paid for.
risks.entitlement_changed: Changing what “{{product}}” unlocks affects people who already bought it.

apply.nothing: Nothing has changed since the last time.

steps.code: Claude is adding the purchases to your app…

apply.failed: This didn’t work and your app was put back as it was.

missing.product_problems: Fix the products that have a problem.
missing.gating_not_approved: Approve the plan for what goes behind the paywall.
missing.secret_apple: Add your App Store Connect key.

confirm.titleUpdate: Update the purchases in your app?
confirm.permanent: These product IDs are permanent in the stores:
confirm.deleteLimits: Products in the stores can’t always be deleted again, and Apple and Google keep their IDs for good.
confirm.snapshotNote: Studio saves a snapshot first and checks the app afterwards. If something fails, everything is put back.
confirm.paid_apps_agreement: The paid apps agreement is accepted (App Store)
confirm.paid_apps_agreementHelp: In App Store Connect under Business. Without it, purchases can’t be sold.
confirm.tax_bank: Tax and bank details are filled in (App Store)
confirm.tax_bankHelp: Also under Business in App Store Connect.
confirm.merchant_account: A merchant account is set up (Google Play)
confirm.merchant_accountHelp: In Play Console under Setup, payments profile.
confirm.sandbox_tested: I tried a test purchase on a real phone
confirm.sandbox_testedHelp: Use a sandbox tester (Apple) or a license tester (Google). Studio never makes real purchases in its own test run.
confirm.apple_submitted: The first purchase was submitted with an app version (App Store)
confirm.apple_submittedHelp: Apple reviews the first in-app purchase together with an app version.

remove.title: Remove “{{name}}”?
remove.body: This product is already in your app or a store. Removing it here takes it out of your app at the next update, but the stores keep it, and people who bought it keep access.

profile.working: Getting Claude ready for this project…

dev.title: Developer mode
dev.on: Developer mode is on. Click the version line five more times to turn it off.

metrics.levels: At the start: small {{small}}, screen {{screen}}, shared {{shared}}, project {{project}}

apple.name: Apple (App Store)
apple.desc: Lets Studio upload your iPhone app to App Store Connect.

issuer_id.label: Issuer ID
issuer_id.help: The long ID shown at the top of the App Store Connect API page (Users and Access, Integrations). It looks like 69a6de7e-….

key_id.label: Key ID
key_id.help: The 10-character ID next to your key in the same table.

team_id.label: Team ID
team_id.help: 10 characters, shown in your Apple Developer account under Membership details.

private_key.label: API key file (.p8)
private_key.help: Apple lets you download this file only once. Store it here right away; if it is lost you must create a new key.

google_play.name: Google Play
google_play.desc: Everything for Android publishing: your Google Play connection and the key that signs your app.

service_account.label: Service account key (JSON)
service_account.help: Create a service account in Google Cloud, add a JSON key, then invite its email address in Play Console under Users and permissions.

keystore.label: Upload keystore
keystore.help: Studio can create this for you. Make a backup: if the keystore is lost, you can no longer update your published app.

alias.label: Key alias
alias.help: The name of the key inside the keystore. Studio uses "upload" when it creates the keystore.

keystore_password.label: Keystore password
keystore_password.help: Studio fills this in when it creates the keystore.

key_password.label: Key password
key_password.help: Only needed if it differs from the keystore password.

supabase.name: Supabase
supabase.desc: An online database and login for your app.

url.label: Project URL
url.help: Found in Supabase under Project Settings, Data API. It looks like https://xxxx.supabase.co.

publishable_key.label: Publishable key (public)
publishable_key.help: Safe to put in the app. Starts with sb_publishable_ (older projects: the anon key).

secret_key.label: Secret key
secret_key.help: Full access to your data. Never goes in the app. Starts with sb_secret_ (older projects: the service_role key). Only add it if you need it.

access_token.label: Personal access token
access_token.help: Lets Claude set up tables for you through Supabase. Create it under Account, Access Tokens. Starts with sbp_.

firebase.name: Firebase
firebase.desc: Google's online database and login for your app.

google_services_json.label: google-services.json (Android)
google_services_json.help: Download it from Firebase, Project settings, Your apps. It is not secret, but Studio keeps it with the rest.

google_service_info_plist.label: GoogleService-Info.plist (iPhone)
google_service_info_plist.help: Needed for the iPhone version. Not secret.

service_account.label: Service account key (JSON)
service_account.help: Only for server-side tasks. Full access: keep it private.

local_db.name: Local database
local_db.desc: Data stays on the phone. No account and no secrets needed.

github.name: GitHub
github.desc: Optional: lets Studio back up your project to GitHub.

token.label: Access token
token.help: Create a fine-grained token in GitHub under Settings, Developer settings. Give it access to your project's repository only.

vercel.name: Vercel
vercel.desc: Optional: lets Studio put a web version of your app online.

token.label: Access token
token.help: Create it in Vercel under Account Settings, Tokens.

team_id.label: Team ID
team_id.help: Only if the project belongs to a team. Starts with team_.

purchases.name: In-app purchases (stores)
purchases.desc: Optional extra keys so Studio can set up your products in the App Store and Google Play. The Google Play key from the Google Play card is used too.

apple_iap_key.label: App Store Connect key for purchases (.p8)
apple_iap_key.help: Create it in App Store Connect under Users and Access, Integrations, In-App Purchase. Studio keeps it in your keychain.

apple_iap_key_id.label: Key ID
apple_iap_key_id.help: The 10 letters and digits shown next to the key in App Store Connect.

revenuecat.name: RevenueCat
revenuecat.desc: Handles renewals, restoring purchases and who has access to what. Recommended for subscriptions.

public_sdk_key.label: Public SDK key
public_sdk_key.help: In RevenueCat under Project settings, API keys. It starts with appl_ or goog_.

secret_api_key.label: Secret API key (optional)
secret_api_key.help: Only needed if Studio should create products and offerings in RevenueCat for you. It starts with sk_.

tasks.title: Background tasks
tasks.done: Done. You can see what changed in the chat or under Versions.
tasks.cancelled: Stopped. Nothing was changed after the last snapshot.
tasks.failed: This didn’t work. You can try again.

update.title: Studio {{version}} is available
update.body: You have version {{current}}. Update now to get the latest improvements. Studio restarts when it’s done; your projects stay as they are.
update.failed: The update didn’t work. Check your internet connection and try again.
